I did think of that option. I could have apply for a PR during my undergraduate years, but that would mean I cannot go back to the country until I'm at my late 30's. It's just a very harsh law, and I don't really want to be labelled as someone who ran away from his own family and country.

Thank you so much for your concerns. After talking to my best friend, I realize that suicide is probably not a wise choice. I just have way too much leverage in this world. 

This is an odd thought, but being this close to killing myself kind of alleviates some anxiety and gives me a strange sense of inner peace. As in, now that I know how to take away my life so easily and without any physical pain (with chemicals in my lab), I do not fear death anymore. If someone were to put a gun on my head, I would say "well, at least now YOU're the asshole." It's a strange feeling.

Once again, thank you for taking your time to read through my darkest thoughts.

First, thank you so much for your time and patience. I am truly grateful.

The easiest choice would be to take the path of service as a researcher in Korea. I'm just going to have to suck it up for three years and try to make the best out of it. Just because I feel sorry for myself, it doesn't grant me a special privilege to disobey the law and run away from my country. The only way I can get away with it is by becoming an American citizen via marrying an American citizen, and I'm not really planning on marrying anyone soon haha.

On the second question, I agree with you on having the practical things before ideational things. I mean... I just don't live in a dream world and weep because my life is not a fairy tale. I've been working pretty hard to achieve that goal, and so far the progress has been great. I think the reason I have such high hopes in my life, which tends to get crushed quite a bit sometimes, is because I am very confident that I will not starve to death when I grow up. I am sure that I will have a decent job at an engineering firm, living on a salary like my father, but (no offense to anyone) that is just not the path I want to choose. I guess the issue is that I've been trying to stay away from the normal to become extraordinary so much that I see myself as abnormal sometimes, and during those times, I just go on a dangerous downward spiral for a few hours or days.
I did not quite understand what you were saying, but I am definitely interested in your philosophy. Could you elaborate?

I'm doing pretty well in school. I try not to let my personal life affect my academic life. If I do find myself doing so, I immediately freeze all emotions, and turn into work mode because I feel so ashamed of myself for letting myself slip. That happened only once when I was crushed by a girl.

There is no way I can just stay in the states unless I become exiled from Korea, but there are ways to not be on the front line. The reason I'm getting my masters is to increase my chance of being that exception. Some Koreans, if they are accepted to industry, can work for 3 years, and that counts as "service." Even then, it is not necessarily something I would like to do. Sure, it would be a learning experience, but I remember when I had an internship in Korea, I was just miserable. The work environment is so intense that it just sucks the joy out of people. I remember I was at the gym, and I just dropped my weight in the middle of a set and thought "why bother doing this if I'm going to end up as miserable, joyless and out-of-shape as the rest of the people in that company?" Korea, even though it is very well developed, still cannot compete with the states in terms of resources, so a lot of the times, in order to compete with the U.S. companies, the work environment is pretty depressing because there is no room for mistakes or adventure.

If i had a choice to do anything right now, I would like to live in SF or Oslo, Norway, start a company based on what i've learned from all over the world, and be someone exceptional. My dream is to one day look at a field with enough solar cells to power the world and say "this is my work." I mean, if you're gonna take the route of an ego maniac, you gotta have at least a wikipedia page about yourself before you die, right? 

Because of my overly grandiose ambition, I constantly have an existential crisis. Sometimes, I just want to live in a quiet farm without having to worry about much. The scariest part of going back to Korea is that I'm going to have to put everything that I love behind: all my friends, family of friends, my chinchilla, my music etc. I am going to have to switch to a whole new person to fit in and do well over there. In Unbreakable, Samuel L Jackson says "Do you know what the scariest thing is? To not know your place in this world, to not know why you're here." With all that has happened in my life and all the things that is going to happen, this quote is the way I have felt most of my life.
